summary:
TerraTwin is an interactive 3D planetary exploration and decision-support platform designed to identify Earth locations with terrain characteristics similar to selected regions on the Moon and Mars. The project addresses the challenge of evaluating potential sites for future permanent settlements by bringing planetary comparison, mission priorities, and geospatial visualization into one environment.

Users can select a lunar or Martian target region, define mission-specific criteria, and explore ranked Earth analog candidates. The platform scans 11,469 Earth candidate coordinate cells and presents comparison results through 3D planetary visualization, radar charts, terrain cross-sections, and explainable analysis reports.

By connecting Earth's geographical diversity with lunar and Martian exploration, TerraTwin makes complex spatial information more accessible and easier to interpret. It aims to support researchers and mission-planning teams in preliminary site assessment, helping them explore potential locations and identify areas that deserve further investigation.
details:
TerraTwin is a 3D planetary exploration and mission-planning platform designed to compare potential settlement regions on the Moon and Mars with geographically similar locations on Earth.

Users select a target region on the Moon or Mars and define mission priorities using predefined profiles or custom criteria. The system scans 11,469 candidate coordinate cells across Earth to identify potential analog locations. It evaluates terrain characteristics such as slope, elevation, relief, and image-derived surface features. When available, elevation data and NASA POWER climate information provide additional environmental context.

The platform presents the top three Earth analog candidates, complementary locations, and cross-comparisons between the Moon and Mars. Results can be explored through interactive 3D planetary visualizations, radar charts, terrain cross-sections, and explainable analysis reports. Users can also export their results in several formats.

TerraTwin aims to make planetary analog research more accessible and mission-oriented. By connecting Earth's geographical diversity with lunar and Martian exploration, it helps researchers identify regions worth investigating further and supports preliminary site assessment.

The project was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, and Three.js for the frontend and 3D visualization, with Python, NumPy, SciPy, OpenCV, and Pillow for backend processing and analysis. It also incorporates planetary imagery and contextual data sources such as NASA GIBS, Copernicus DEM, NASA SRTM, and NASA POWER. The system references lunar and Martian measurement datasets, including LOLA and MOLA, for cataloged target information.

TerraTwin's innovative approach combines Earth analog matching, adjustable mission priorities, cross-planet comparisons, and explainable visual analysis in one interactive platform. During development, our team considered terrain characteristics, mission requirements, data reliability, comparability, usability, and transparency. The platform distinguishes measured information from image-derived indicators and preliminary estimates.

Ultimately, TerraTwin is designed as a decision-support tool that transforms complex planetary information into accessible comparative insights, helping researchers explore potential locations for future human missions.
